tldr: Headlines from virtually every region deploy Trump's 'last chance before decapitation' formulation verbatim, making the military-threat register the most uniform headline layer in this corpus. A secondary cluster — led by Egyptian, Turkish, Canadian, and pan-Arab outlets — foregrounds the diplomatic contradiction (Iran flatly denying talks Trump insists are ongoing) rather than the threat itself. Iran state media alone opts out of both registers entirely, presenting a routine bilateral Oman–Iran Hormuz shipping negotiation with no reference to decapitation, strikes, or US talks.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only outlet in the corpus to lead with Trump's cancellation of strikes ('Trump cancels planned attack on Iran'), casting the US as the de-escalating party rather than the issuer of ultimatums — the inverse angle of every other headline, which foregrounds 'last chance' or 'decapitation.'

The only outlet to surface the parallel military-planning track: US Central Command soliciting 'creative, unconventional ways' to punish Iran — a headline framing that contradicts the peace-talk narrative dominant across all other titles and absent from any other outlet's homepage.

The only outlet to lead with the energy-market dimension ('Aramco sidesteps Hormuz as Iran crisis cuts flows to a tenth'), foregrounding global supply disruption rather than the diplomatic-military standoff — a frame absent from every other title in the corpus.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the US-Iran standoff is flattened almost universally to Trump's 'last chance before decapitation' formulation; the diplomatic contradiction (Iran denying talks) surfaces as a secondary frame across Egyptian, Turkish, Canadian, and pan-Arab outlets, while Iran state media alone defects from both narratives to present a routine bilateral Hormuz shipping negotiation.
